source_note: BLS OEWS May 2025 national estimates, pulled from the BLS Public Data API (series OEUN0000000000000<SOC><datatype>) on 2026-10-16.

occupations.title: Graphic Designer
occupations.units: per project or per deliverable (logo package, brand guide, social template set), with an hourly rate kept for revisions beyond the agreed rounds
occupations.covers: people who plan and create visual concepts for print and digital media: logos, layouts, packaging, marketing materials
occupations.tip: Write the number of revision rounds into the quote. Extra rounds are where design projects quietly lose money.

occupations.title: Web Developer
occupations.units: per project for builds, plus a monthly retainer or hourly rate for maintenance and change requests
occupations.covers: people who build and maintain websites and web applications, including code, performance and site functionality
occupations.tip: Separate the build quote from ongoing maintenance. A retainer for updates and fixes smooths income between projects.

occupations.title: Web & Digital Interface Designer
occupations.units: per project or per phase (research, wireframes, visual design, handoff)
occupations.covers: people who design the look, layout and usability of websites and app interfaces
occupations.tip: Phase-based quotes let a client approve wireframes before you invest hours in polished screens.

occupations.title: Technical Writer
occupations.units: per hour or per document/page set, with subject-matter interviews billed as time
occupations.covers: people who write instruction manuals, how-to guides, documentation and other supporting material
occupations.tip: Interview and review time with engineers is real work. Quote it explicitly instead of folding it into a per-page price.

occupations.title: Writer
occupations.units: per word, per article or per project; convert any per-word offer back to an hourly figure before accepting
occupations.covers: people who write original content for books, websites, advertising, scripts and other media
occupations.tip: Track how many words you actually finish per hour, including research and edits, so per-word offers can be checked against your floor.

occupations.title: Editor
occupations.units: per word or per page for copyediting and proofreading, per hour for developmental or structural editing
occupations.covers: people who plan, review and revise content for publication
occupations.tip: Ask for a sample chapter or page before quoting; the condition of the manuscript changes your hourly pace a lot.

occupations.title: Photographer
occupations.units: per session or per day, with editing time, travel and usage/licensing priced as separate lines
occupations.covers: people who photograph people, products, events and places
occupations.tip: A one-hour shoot often needs several more hours of prep, travel, culling and editing. Price the whole job, not the shutter time.

occupations.title: Translator & Interpreter
occupations.units: per word for written translation (often with a minimum fee), per hour or half-day for interpreting
occupations.covers: people who convert written or spoken information from one language into another
occupations.tip: Set a minimum fee for small jobs. A 150-word translation still needs setup, terminology checks and delivery.

occupations.title: Bookkeeper
occupations.units: monthly fixed fee based on transaction volume and number of accounts, with catch-up work quoted separately
occupations.covers: people who record financial transactions, update records and check them for accuracy
occupations.tip: Price by monthly transaction volume and accounts reconciled, and quote clean-up of messy back months as a separate project.

occupations.title: Video Editor
occupations.units: per finished minute or per project, with revision rounds and stock/music licences listed separately
occupations.covers: people who edit raw footage into finished film, video and broadcast content
occupations.tip: Footage volume drives the hours. Ask how much raw footage there is before quoting a per-minute price.

occupations.title: Animator
occupations.units: per second or per finished minute of animation, or per project with storyboard approval as a paid first phase
occupations.covers: people who create animation and visual effects for film, video, games and other media
occupations.tip: Make the storyboard or animatic a paid, signed-off phase so changes after approval are billable.

occupations.title: Marketing Specialist
occupations.plural: market research analysts and marketing specialists
occupations.units: monthly retainer for ongoing work, per project for audits, strategies and campaign setups
occupations.covers: people who research market conditions and plan or run marketing campaigns
occupations.tip: Define deliverables per month in a retainer (reports, campaigns, hours) so scope does not creep.
